title: TCP LoadBalancer proxyProtocol option deprecated

detection.reason: the proxyProtocol setting lives on a service under spec.routes[].services[], nested inside the routes array rather than at the top level of the projection

quote: Starting with `v3.5.2`, the `proxyProtocol` option for TCP LoadBalancer is deprecated. This option can now be configured at the `TCPServersTransport` level, please check out the documentation for more details.
remediation: Move `proxyProtocol` from the TCP service definition to a `TCPServersTransport`. Getting this wrong is not silent — a backend expecting the PROXY protocol header and not receiving it (or receiving it unexpectedly) fails the connection outright.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutetcps.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]?.services[]? | select(.proxyProtocol != null) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name' # names printed still set proxyProtocol on the service

title: TLS certificate expiry metric renamed to seconds

detection.reason: this concerns Traefik's own metrics output, which this platform does not scrape

quote: Starting with `v3.5.4`, and when using OpenTelemetry, the `traefik_tls_certs_not_after_milliseconds` metric is renamed to `traefik_tls_certs_not_after_seconds`. This change aligns the metric name with its real unit precision, which is in seconds.
remediation: Update any dashboard or alert using `traefik_tls_certs_not_after_milliseconds` to the `_seconds` name. Certificate-expiry alerting is exactly the kind that fails silently — the query stops returning data and the alert simply never fires.

title: traceVerbosity defaults to minimal, producing fewer spans

detection.reason: this is Traefik static or provider configuration, not a field on any collected Kubernetes object

quote: Starting with `v3.5.0`, a new `traceVerbosity` option is available for both entrypoints and routers. This option allows you to control the level of detail for tracing spans.
remediation: If you rely on tracing, set `traceVerbosity` explicitly. Existing configurations default to `minimal`, which produces fewer spans than before — one server span and one client span per request. Traces will look thinner after the upgrade without anything appearing to fail.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)(mirrored-library-|library-)?traefik([:@]|$)"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) replicas=\(.spec.replicas // "per-node")", (.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.args // [])[]), (.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.env // [])[] | "env \(.name)")' | grep -iE '^(Deployment|DaemonSet) |traceVerbosity|tracing' # rows show whether tracing is on and traceVerbosity set; with tracing on and the option unset, traces get thinner (minimal) after the upgrade; a static configuration file mounted from a ConfigMap is not listed, read it too
